# Helm vs ConfigHub — the same bad decisions, but *when do you find out?*

**UNOFFICIAL/EXPERIMENTAL.** Live receipt generated by `scripts/run-bad-decisions-comparison.mjs`; do not hand-edit. Regenerate with `npm run bad-decisions:comparison`.

**Claim.** Same bad decisions, asked WHEN you find out. Raw Helm surfaces only render-rejected decisions before the cluster; leaked values reach the live k8s API at apply and absorbed values silently succeed. Config-as-data renders the same output but surfaces every outcome — change, empty no-op, or render error — as a reviewable diff before apply: 100% at review, 0 silent. (cub does not reject more; the difference is visibility and timing.)

The [careless-dev fuzz](../bad-decisions-fuzz/summary.md) showed Helm's *outcomes*. This runs the **same 180 decisions** (18 types × 10 charts, one corpus in `scripts/lib/bad-decisions.mjs`) and asks **when each is surfaced** — before the cluster, only at the live API, or never.

| When is the bad decision surfaced? | Raw Helm (`--set` → install / Argo-helm) | Config-as-data (cub / ConfigHub) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Before the cluster** (at review/render) | render-rejected only — **2 (1%)** | **all 180 (100%)** — in the reviewed config |
| **Only at the live k8s API** (at apply) | leaked — **60 (33%)** | — (already seen at review) |
| **Never** — silent success | absorbed — **118 (66%)** | — (a visible no-op edit) |

Overall: **pass** (0 unclassified). **Headline:** for the same decisions, raw Helm surfaces **1%** before the cluster; config-as-data surfaces **100%** at review (a concrete change, an empty no-op, or a render error) — *before* anything is applied.

## The honest nuance

cub does **not** reject more than Helm — it renders with the same engine, so the rejected/leaked/absorbed split (2/60/118) is identical (and matches the fuzz). The win is **visibility and timing**: a leaked value sits **in the config you review** instead of surfacing as a surprise at apply, and an absorbed value is a **visible no-op edit** — you set a key the chart ignores, which you can see in your config, instead of a silently successful install. Config-as-data *surfaces* the decision at review; a human still has to read it.
